_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local nodes for band4_upper_meadows_ironwood. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order harvest nodes are added to the scene tree. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 4000-4999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.
_comment_ironwood_d4: GATE-D4/prompt 65. Ironwood is Band 4's whole material tier (spec Band 4, `data/recipes/recipes_ironwood.json`) and this file held zero nodes at package start -- the only ironwood anywhere in the chapter was five nodes in `data/config/bands/band2_stone_and_root/harvest.json`, sited around the Burrow Warrens, a Band 2 site the D2 lane owns and this lane does not touch. A player who reaches Band 4's captains without having taken the Warrens spur had no ironwood at all, and one who had could not restock without a ~2km walk back through a region already cleared. These five nodes put the tier where spec Band 4 actually names it: the old-growth on the western swing, the same pocket `spawns.json`'s order-4000 trailpup cluster already sites, so gathering the region's own resource happens inside the region's own old-growth rather than a neighbour's dungeon. MEASURED with `tools/_probe_band4_sites.gd` (heights 1.3-3.8m, worst local slope 5.3-9.1 degrees over a 3m pad -- the five flattest of eight candidates walked across the same old-growth pocket). Model/scale pattern matches band2's own ironwood nodes (`TwistedTree_1/2/3`, ~0.28-0.32) so the two stands read as the same species rather than two different trees that both happen to drop the same item. Amounts and scales TUNABLE.
_comment_stand_d4b: GATE-D4b, round 1 of the blind visual pass (ralph/conventions.md). The critic, shown shots/band4/ and nothing about what changed, named this stand twice: `ironwood-grove does not read as a grove -- four isolated trees on open lawn', and `constant scale at even intervals ... that is a scatter pass, not a placement'. Both were true of the numbers it was judging: the five nodes stood 35-70m apart in a rough line across the old-growth at model_scale 0.28-0.32, a 14 percent spread that reads as one repeated tree. Re-sited into a clustered stand -- a four-tree core inside ~15m at (-342,5078) (-336,5069) (-352,5074) (-345,5088), with a fifth at (-339,5060) carrying the group south -- so the mass clusters and the ground between the trees reads as a clearing rather than as the default state of the region. Scales spread to 0.26-0.42, an elder tree and a young one in the same stand, still centred on band2's own 0.28-0.32 so the two ironwood stands stay the same species rather than becoming two trees that happen to drop the same item. Every position MEASURED with tools/_probe_band4_sites.gd (heights 1.48-2.09m, worst local slope 3.0-9.1 degrees over a 2m pad -- the five flattest of twelve candidates walked across the pocket), all of them 8-25m from clearings[4002]'s camp pad so the fire stands beside the stand it supplies. What the critic named that this does NOT fix is the region's scatter density, which is not this lane's file to edit: see the standing density_scale request in ralph/DONE.md.
_comment_red_leak_d4b: GATE-D4b, round 2 of the blind pass. The critic, given only the frames, wrote `oxblood has leaked onto friendly scenery -- the red ironwood canopies are the largest saturated red mass anywhere in the survey' and `the same asset is two different colours in adjacent frames'. Both are one bug, and the repo already knew it: data/config/vegetation.json's `grove' layer carries `_comment_leak' -- `R9.4. THE RED LEAK, found by two independent blind reviews eleven days apart. Leaves_TwistedTree_C.png is RGB(167,23,23)' -- and retextures those leaves to Leaves_NormalTree_C at #78c86e so the meadow's biggest trees are not blood red. harvest_node.gd::_material_fixups_for_model() applies that same layer data to a harvest node, BY MODEL PATH, and the `grove' layer lists only TwistedTree_2 and TwistedTree_4. So a node built from TwistedTree_1 or _3 gets no fixup at all and renders the pack's raw crimson. This stand was authored from _2, _1 and _3, which is why one stand rendered in two colours and why the red half landed on the one hue spec 21 reserves for Team Tether. Re-authored across TwistedTree_2 and TwistedTree_4 only -- the two forms that actually receive the meadow's own retexture -- keeping two forms and the 0.26-0.42 scale spread, so the stand reads as one species in the Meadows palette. NOT fixed here, and flagged for the coordinator: band2_stone_and_root/harvest.json's five ironwood nodes use _1/_2/_3 and carry the identical leak, and the underlying gap is that a harvest node whose model no scatter layer lists silently gets no material fixup -- both are other lanes' files. GATE-D4b round 3: re-authored again onto TwistedTree_4 ALONE. The grove layer's `variant_retint' is a deliberate three-step family -- TwistedTree_2 takes #325f3c, a deep dark green, and TwistedTree_4 takes #c4d696, a pale yellow-green -- which works across a scattered wood, where the steps average into one canopy, and does not work across a five-tree stand, where three dark and two pale trees are two trees rather than one species. Round 3's blind critic, told nothing, read the result as `bone-white trunks under near-black desaturated canopies ... blight/dead-forest/enemy-territory language, not friendly wilderness', and said a player walking in would assume they had crossed into hostile ground -- the same off-palette failure as the crimson, one variant along. All five nodes now take the pale variant, so the stand is one species in the lit half of the meadow's own green, and the 0.26-0.42 scale spread does the differentiating that model choice was doing badly. The grey bark stays: `Bark_TwistedTree' is untouched by any layer and is what separates an ironwood from the terracotta-trunked trees around it -- species identity carried by the trunk, not by a canopy in the wrong palette.
_comment_landmark_scale_visual_groundcov: VISUAL-GROUNDCOVER. ASSESSMENT_2026-08-23's blind critique measured this stand's trees at orchard scale (6-9m) against the key art board's 15-20m landmark oaks. TwistedTree_4's own raw height is 18.74m (tools/measure_models.gd) so the previous 0.26-0.42 model_scale span put every node at 4.9-7.9m -- exactly that orchard reading, on the one species this band names in its own title. Two of the five nodes (4000, 4003) are raised toward the keyart's 15-20m band, modest scale variation rather than uniformly regrading the whole stand: `_comment_stand_d4b` above already fixed 'four isolated trees on open lawn' by making these read as one clustered stand with an elder/young spread, and turning every tree into a landmark would undo that same finding by making all five compete for the eye instead of one or two anchoring the group while the rest read as its younger understorey. No new asset -- same TwistedTree_4/pale-variant fixup this stand already used, per `_comment_red_leak_d4b` round 3.
